title: unit-cost-logbook-model-calibration-review
content:
Purpose:
This logbook captures the internal review notes for the unit-cost modeling work: the raw data inputs, the calibration procedures we ran against observed host metrics, the spreadsheet layout we used to calculate per-token and per-request costs, and the current finance sign-off checklist. Goal is to create an auditable trail so engineering, product and finance can reconcile numbers quickly and iterate on next calibration cycles.

Scope and quick summary: 
- Scope: hosted API + dedicated GPU pools cost modeling for text generation and embeddings (primary focus on gen workloads). Excludes one-off infra amortization modeling for on-prem private deployments (tracked in a separate doc).
- Current headline: baseline per-1k-token marginal cost (mixed fleet) = $0.018 (midpoint after batching/kv-cache assumed). This is a working value pending finance sign-off.

1) Data sources inventory (provenance notes)
- Scheduler logs (serving-runtime): sample window 2025-01-01 to 2025-01-31; extracted via internal export job scheduler-export-202501. Quality: high coverage for hosted, partial for Dedicated (missing some burst traces). Stored in S3: s3://redwood-prod-exports/optimize/2025-01/scheduler.csv.
- Billing CSVs (cloud invoices): AWS & GCP monthly invoices Jan 2025 consolidated by FinOps. File id: FIN-INVOICE-2025-01 (attached in Finance workspace). Caveat: invoices include egress/managed services; we strip non-inference line items per invoice-mapping-v2.xlsx.
- GPU telemetry (nvidia/prometheus): 1s-sampled traces for utilization and power draw. Aggregated via infra-metrics/telemetry-processor v0.9.2. Known issue: some Dedicated hosts had missing telemetry due to agent bug (agent-1.5.7) between 2025-01-09 and 2025-01-12.
- Request-level logs (api-proxy): sample of 10M requests for Jan 2025. Contains prompt tokens, response tokens, model variant, route id. Exported with redaction; no PII.
- Benchmarks / perf matrix: internal bench harness runs (benchmark-suite/alpha) for candidate quantized models. Multiple runs per seed; latest run 2025-02-05.

Provenance priorities and transformations applied: 
- Token counts derived from request-level logs; we apply whitespace-norm and tokenization: redwood-tokenizer-v2.2 to match serving runtime.
- GPU cost allocation uses time-weighted allocation: for mixed workloads we attribute cost by GPU-minutes spent by model variant.
- Amortization: node purchasing amortized over 36 months by default; hardware refresh schedule is captured in infra-capex-2024.xlsx.

2) Calibration procedure and notes
- Objective: align modeled per-token costs with observed monthly spend within +/- 5% for hosted API and within +/- 8% for Dedicated pools.
- Steps taken: 
  * Step A: baseline run using naive assumptions (no batching, no cache) to validate raw per-token kernel cost mapping to GPU-minutes.
  * Step B: introduce batching model: use empirical batch size distribution from request logs (p50=1, p75=4, p95=16). Use continuous-batching model with latency-SLO constraints to compute effective tokens/sec.
  * Step C: apply prefix/KV caching hit-rates derived from route traces; measured median cache hit = 12% for chat-like routes; apply this as token reduction factor per request.
  * Step D: apply quantization efficiency multipliers from benchmark-suite (e.g., 4-bit q4 models show ~1.9x lower GPU-seconds per token vs fp16 on A100).
- Tunable params we hand-calibrated: batch_eff_factor (0.65–0.9), kv_cache_hit (0.08–0.2), quantization_speedup (1.6–2.1). Chosen default for modeling: batch_eff=0.78, kv_cache_hit=0.12, quant_speedup=1.9.
- Calibration runs and residuals:
  * Run 2025-02-10. Delta to invoice: +3.4% (hosted), -5.1% (Dedicated).
  * Run 2025-02-18 (adjusted batch_eff to 0.72): Delta: +0.9% (hosted), -3.2% (Dedicated).
  * Run 2025-02-25 (applied corrected telemetry patch for missing Dedicated hosts): Delta: +1.2% (hosted), +0.4% (Dedicated).
- Conclusion: last calibration (2025-02-25) within target band. We recommend re-running monthly or after any fleet change.

3) Spreadsheet mapping (how the sheet is organized and formulas in plain English)
- Sheet name used: unit_cost_model_v3.xlsx (tab: summary, tab: detail_by_route, tab: assumptions, tab: data_provenance).
- Key columns (detail_by_route): route_id, model_variant, requests, avg_input_tokens, avg_output_tokens, total_tokens = requests * (avg_input + avg_output), effective_tokens = total_tokens * (1 - kv_cache_hit), gpu_seconds = effective_tokens / effective_tps, infra_cost = gpu_seconds * gpu_cost_per_second + node_overheads, amortized_cost = infra_cost + infra_capex_monthly_alloc, per_request_cost = amortized_cost / requests, per_1k_tokens = per_request_cost * 1000 / (avg_input+avg_output).
- Formulas: references use named ranges (gpu_cost_per_second, effective_tps_by_variant, kv_cache_hit_by_route). We avoid embedding magic numbers; all tunable knobs live in assumptions tab.

4) Key assumptions (explicit, with rationale)
- gpu_cost_per_second: $0.0012 (blended across instance types). Rationale: derived from cloud invoices after allocating shared services and storage; see invoice mapping sheet. Sensitivity: a 10% change in this value changes per-1k-token by ~8%.
- effective_tps_by_variant: measured on benchmarks; e.g., gpt-like-13b-q4 => 120 tokens/sec at seq=1024 median. Rationale: bench harness median across 5 runs; we use median to avoid outliers.
- kv_cache_hit default: 12% (see above). Rationale: empirical from route traces; sensitive for chat/assistant routes.
- amortization_months: 36 (default). Rationale: standard infra practice; finance can change to 24/48 for different pools.

5) Known gaps, outstanding risks, and mitigations
- Gap: Dedicated burst traces are incomplete for 2025-01 due to telemetry agent bug. Mitigation: we patched logs and re-ran capture for Feb; recommended to apply conservative +3% buffer for Dedicated until full continuous capture is validated.
- Gap: Egress and non-inference cloud charges sometimes bleed into inference buckets in invoices. Mitigation: finance to supply finalized mapping table (invoice-mapping-v3) before sign-off.
- Risk: Model architecture changes (new kernels, fused attention) can materially alter effective_tps. Mitigation: require bench run with production-like input shapes and seed tests before flipping recommended quantization/variant in the pricing table.

6) Finance sign-off checklist (current status columns in sheet: required/owner/status/notes)
- [ ] Confirm final invoice mapping for Jan 2025 (owner: Priya Desai, status: in_progress)
- [x] Validate amortization policy (owner: Infra-Fin, status: done, note: 36 months approved)
- [ ] Agree on batch_eff defaults for hosted vs dedicated (owner: Maya Patel + Eng-SRE, status: in_review)
- [ ] Approve quantization speedup multipliers for listed model variants (owner: R&D + Finance, status: in_review)
- [ ] Formal sign-off meeting scheduled (owner: Priya Desai) — tentative 2025-03-05
- Required acceptance criteria: modeled monthly cost within +/-5% of consolidated invoices and documented sensitivity grid attached.

7) Decision log (key entries)
- 2025-02-12: Chose 36-month amortization (reason: align with infra-capex policy). 
- 2025-02-18: Adjusted batch_eff default from 0.78 -> 0.72 after p95 latency analysis for hosted API.
- 2025-02-25: Accepted corrected telemetry import; re-run matched invoices to +0.4% for Dedicated.

8) Action items / next steps
- Finance (Priya): provide invoice-mapping-v3 and confirm non-inference exclusions by 2025-03-03.
- Eng-SRE (Ethan): validate telemetry agent across Dedicated fleet (target 2025-03-07) and publish a corrected export.
- Product (Maya): run one additional calibration pass after final mapping and prepare short one-pager for exec showback (due 2025-03-09).
- Research (Rina): run benchmark-suite on next-gen kernels with seq=2048 shapes and provide updated effective_tps by 2025-03-14.

9) Unresolved questions (for meeting)
- Do we adopt a separate amortization schedule for older Dedicated pools (they were purchased in 2021)?
- What guardrails should we require before recommending quantized variant for customer-facing default (A/B rollout threshold)?
- How conservative should we be about reserve capacity in cost model when recommending Dedicated commit sizes?

Appendix: quick references / where artifacts live
- unit_cost_model_v3.xlsx: gdrive://product/optimize/unit_cost_model_v3.xlsx
- Raw exports: s3://redwood-prod-exports/optimize/2025-01/
- Bench harness: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmark-suite (PR-78 contains q4-run configs)
- Infra-capex schedule: gdrive://finance/infra-capex-2024.xlsx

Notes to reviewers: please add inline comments in the spreadsheet (tab assumptions) for any proposed changes to multipliers or amortization. If you want a deeper reconciliation, tag Ethan and Priya and ask for a joint session — 30 min should suffice.

Signed-off-by: Maya Patel (product-optimize)
